title: Step tracing and quality numbers

story: Friday, weekly run review. The run in which Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, worked on RH-1234 cost $4.10, about twice what a small frontend ticket usually costs, and someone asks the obvious question: where did the money go? The LLM gateway, the service every model call passes through, knows the total. It does not know whether the plan took three tries, or the build ran the same failing test twenty times, because every call of the run looks the same.

The next ticket on the list is worse. Its run failed in the build step because the change needed a shared helper that the plan never mentioned. The build is where it broke, but the plan is where it should have been caught. If nobody writes that down the same way every week, the same mistake comes back next month and looks new.
hook.question: How do we see what each step of a run spent, and which step should have caught a problem, without adding code inside the agent?

read.h: Five tags on everything a step sends
p: A Nova run moves through nine steps, always in this order: ticket, plan, plan_ok, vm, build, pr, byte, approve and learn. The steps that talk to Claude each run as their own Agent SDK session, a separate Claude conversation with its own process. That gives us a natural place to attach a label: everything one session sends belongs to one step.

So every signal of a step carries the same five tags: agent (nova), jira (RH-1234), run (this run's ID), step (build) and harness.version, the version number of the harness, our program that runs the sessions inside the VM. The same five appear in three places. On Claude Code's own metrics and events, they are resource attributes, the labels a process puts on everything it sends. On every call through the gateway, the step and the version travel as headers, and agent, ticket and run are already inside the run token, the short-lived token the run uses instead of a key. Temporal, the workflow engine that drives each run, gets Step and HarnessVersion as search attributes: fields on the run that the Temporal UI can filter by. Because the names are the same everywhere, cost by step in Grafana must add up to the run's total at the gateway, and checking that sum is the test that tracing works.

The version tag matters most on the day a harness release goes wrong. If build-step cost doubles on Tuesday, split it by harness.version: if only runs on the new version are expensive, you know which pull request to read.

notes.text: The nine steps as a fixed list. as const makes Step a union type, so stepEnv(run, "biuld") fails to compile.
The standard OpenTelemetry variable: name=value pairs separated by commas. Every OpenTelemetry SDK reads it at start, Claude Code included.
Claude Code adds these headers to every model request, so the gateway can label its own token and cost counters with the step.

read.h: Set by the environment, not by the agent
p: Nothing inside the agent knows about the tags. The harness builds the environment of each session and passes it in through the options.env field of the SDK's query() call. Claude Code reads OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES once, when its process starts, and from then on every number and event it sends carries the five tags. That is also why each step must be its own session: a process cannot change its labels halfway, so a single session for the whole run would put every dollar on the first step.

There is one trap, and many people hit it. options.env does not add to the session's environment; it replaces it. If the harness passes only the step's variables, the session loses everything else it had, including the gateway's address and the run token, and it can no longer reach Claude at all. So the harness always spreads process.env first and puts the step's variables on top.

notes.text: process.env first (gateway URL, run token, PATH), then the five tags on top. Leave out the spread and the session starts with nothing but the tags.
A new query() call is a new session, with the environment it was given at the start.

deeper.h: Go deeper: the same tags in Temporal
p: The workflow that drives the run sets two Temporal search attributes, Step and HarnessVersion, each time the run enters a new step. Search attributes are typed, indexed fields on a workflow run; you define each key once with defineSearchAttributeKey and set it with upsertSearchAttributes, which is typed, so a wrong value type fails at compile time. With them, a query in the Temporal UI such as HarnessVersion = "0.5.0" AND Step = "build" lists the runs that are building on the new release right now.

Tags make the weekly run review possible. Each week, someone opens five runs: two at random and the three worst. For every failed or rejected run they write a run label with a small command: the step where it failed, the step that should have caught it, and a cause from a fixed list (too many tools, a bad hand-off between steps, a prompt that contradicts itself, missing context, a flaky environment, the model, or unknown). The lists are fixed on purpose, because labels can only be counted when everyone writes them the same way. The nightly job counts them, and a label seen twice in a month becomes a ticket for a new check, lint rule or skill line.

The same nightly job computes one quality number for each step's gate, the check that a step must pass before the next one starts. Ready on first try: how many tickets passed the readiness check (one cheap model call that decides whether a ticket is clear enough to start) without being sent back. First-pass green: whether the required checks were green on the PR's first push. Caught before the PR: the share of important problems the self-review fixed before Byte, our review agent, found any. Each number shows a weak gate before the end result does. Approvals given less than 60 seconds after the request are listed for the review, never scored: they flag a run, not a person.

lab.title: Split one run's cost by step
lab.goal: Run five fake sessions of one Nova run, each with its own step tags in the environment, and show that cost by step adds up to the run's total.

guess.q: A teammate suggests one session for the whole run: the harness would just change OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES before each step. What would cost by step show?

options.text: The right cost for every step, because the variable is changed before each step starts.
options.why: A process reads its environment once, when it starts. Changing the variable later does not change the labels it already has.

options.text: Nothing at all, because the session would crash when the variable changes.
options.why: Nothing crashes. The danger is quieter: numbers that look fine and are wrong.

options.text: The whole run's cost under the first step, because the labels are fixed when the process starts.
options.why: That is why each step is its own session: a new process reads the new tags.

follow.say: Make a folder and install three OpenTelemetry packages: the metrics SDK, the resource helpers and the exporter that sends protobuf over HTTP, the same format Claude Code uses with our settings. The version in package.json plays the harness version.

npm install @opentelemetry/sdk-metrics@2.11.0 @opentelemetry/resources@2.11.0 @opentelemetry/exporter-metrics-otlp-proto@0.222.0

lab.build: Ship harness 0.5.0, which (we pretend) makes the build step cheaper. Run npm pkg set version=0.5.0, change the build cost in run.mjs from 2.95 to 1.80, and run the harness for another ticket: the same environment variables and node run.mjs RH-1240. Then write the query a reviewer would use on Tuesday: build-step cost split by harness version. Keep last_over_time(...[1h]) from the step query, and wait 30 seconds before you ask.

Cost by step for RH-1234 shows build 2.95, learn 0.14, plan 0.62, pr 0.31 and ticket 0.08, which add up to 4.10.
The build series carries agent, jira, run, step and harness_version labels.
Your version query shows two lines: 0.4.1 with 2.95 and 0.5.0 with 1.8.
In Fix it, every step fails with "no GATEWAY_URL" until you put the spread back.

Make the tidied copy with sed 's/{ ...process.env, ...stepEnv(run, step) }/stepEnv(run, step)/' run.mjs > fix-run.mjs, then run it with the same two variables: node fix-run.mjs RH-1300. Every step fails, and the gateway sees $0.00. Explain why the session lost its gateway address although the harness had it, and repair fix-run.mjs.

check.q: Cost by step for one run adds up to $3.20, but the gateway's total for the run is $4.10. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: One step ran a session without the step tags, so its cost has no step
options.why: Every tagged dollar lands on a step. Money that is missing from the sum was spent by a session that did not get stepEnv.

options.text: The gateway counts cache reads twice
options.why: Both numbers come from the same model calls. A gap between them points at tagging, not at counting.

options.text: The database rounds small numbers away
options.why: $0.90 is not a rounding error. Something spent money without the labels.

check.q: A run failed in the build step because the plan never mentioned a shared helper the change needed. How is it labelled?

options.text: failed_at plan, should_have_caught build, cause model
options.why: That swaps the two steps. It broke in the build; the plan is where it should have been stopped.

options.text: failed_at build, should_have_caught plan, cause missing_context
options.why: Where it broke, where it should have been caught, and why. Seen twice in a month, this label becomes a new check on plans.

options.text: failed_at build, should_have_caught build, cause unknown
options.why: The cause is known: the plan lacked the context. "unknown" is for runs nobody can explain, and it teaches nothing.

check.q: Why is the harness version one of the five tags?

options.text: So the dashboards can show which engineer released the harness
options.why: No dashboard shows people. The version says which code ran, not who wrote it.

options.text: Because Temporal refuses runs without a version
options.why: Temporal needs no such thing. The version is for us, to compare releases.

options.text: So live runs and evals can be split by release, and a regression points at the release that caused it
options.why: If build-step cost doubles only on the new version, you know which change to read.

p: ai-agents/harness/src/telemetry.ts exports STEPS, HARNESS_VERSION (read from harness/package.json) and stepEnv. Every step passes env: { ...process.env, ...stepEnv(run, step) } to query(), with no maxTurns or budget option, because the far-away cost backstop acts between turns in the harness. The gateway already reads x-ai-agents-step and labels ai_agents_llm_tokens_total and ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total with the step. The workflow sets the Step and HarnessVersion search attributes. The check is one dogfood run where cost by step in Grafana equals the run's gateway total.

The weekly run review uses ai-agents/harness/src/label-run.ts (npx tsx harness/src/label-run.ts <run-id> --failed-at … --should-have-caught … --cause …), which writes runs/<run>/label.json to the rhino-ai-agents-eval-results bucket; the nightly job counts labels into ai_agents_run_failures_total{failed_at, should_have_caught, cause} for a panel on the operations dashboard. metrics/src/quality.ts adds delivery_ready_first_try_ratio, delivery_plan_unplanned_files, delivery_plan_items_not_done, delivery_first_pass_green_ratio and delivery_caught_before_pr_ratio per agent and week, as a "Quality at every step" row on the delivery dashboard, and posts approvals under 60 seconds to the review thread.

tickets.why: stepEnv, the five tags on OTel, the gateway and Temporal, and the cost-adds-up check.
The run label command and the weekly review that turns repeated labels into tickets.
One quality number per step's gate, and the list of fast approvals.

words.plain: One of the nine stages of a Nova run. Each step that talks to Claude is its own session.
Labels a process attaches to everything it sends, read from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES when the process starts.
The version number of our harness release, attached to every signal so runs can be compared by release.
Three facts about a failed run: where it failed, which step should have caught it, and a cause from a fixed list.
The check a step must pass before the next step starts, such as the readiness check or green CI.

review.q: Name the five tags and the three places they appear.
review.a: agent, jira, run, step, harness.version; as OTel resource attributes, on gateway calls (step and version as headers, the rest in the run token), and as Temporal search attributes (Step, HarnessVersion).

review.q: What breaks if the harness passes env: stepEnv(run, step) without the spread?
review.a: options.env replaces the whole environment, so the session loses the gateway address and the run token and cannot reach Claude.

review.q: What turns a run label into a change in the platform?
review.a: The nightly job counts labels; one seen twice in a month becomes a ticket for a check, a lint rule or a skill line.

remember: Give each step its own session and the same five tags through its environment, and cost by step adds up to the run's total.
